title: Focus trajectory scratch
body:
Purpose: quick, low-friction tracker for personal outcome signals and micro-OKRs. Not polished — acts as my weekly scratchpad and a place to capture experiments to shift focus and energy.

Context: transitioning to a role that is split across product infra and internal tooling. Need to keep a small set of signals I can actually influence week-to-week. Doing a 4-week experiment to limit my active priorities to 3 measurable outcomes and one deep learning task (reading + notes).

One-line north star (Q4 -> Q1 experiment): increase measurable impact per week by 30% by shrinking context switches and automating two recurring tasks.

Signals (what I track; simple, binary/ratios where possible):
- PR review throughput: PRs reviewed / PRs assigned (target >= 0.8 per week)
- Merge lead time: median hours from ready-for-review -> merged (target <= 24h)
- Meetings flagged as "deep work blocker": count/week (target <= 3)
- Time in focused blocks (90+ minute blocks): hours/week (target >= 6)
- Docs shipped: number of short docs (<= 1 page) shared with team (target >= 1/week)

This week snapshot (W1 of 4 experiment): 2026-03-02 -> 2026-03-08
- PR throughput: 6 reviewed / 7 assigned = 0.86 (good).
- Merge lead time median: 18h (on target).
- Meetings blocking deep work: 4 (1 over target). Two were recurring syncs I should cancel/condense.
- Focus blocks logged: 5 hours (below target). One block was interrupted by pager/infra incident.
- Docs shipped: 1 (roadmap blurb for infra ops).

Wins:
- Put a small gh action to auto-label infra issues created with certain templates — saved ~30m recurring triage time. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-notes/pull/789)
- Experimented with calendar batching: consolidated two 30m syncs into one 60m session — felt less fragmentary.

Blockers / Notes:
- Pager still interrupts morning deep work on Tue. Need to talk to SRE about on-call rotation thresholds (linked INF-482).
- My inbox still uses old triage rules; need to rewrite filters and automate a weekly digest.
- Energy: late-week fatigue reduces focus block effectiveness; might need to shift heavy work earlier in day.

Hypotheses & experiments (A/B-lite):
1) If I designate 3 weekly outcome buckets and refuse to attend non-critical meetings that touch those buckets, then focused time will rise and merge lead time will drop. (Measure: focused hours, merge lead time).
2) If I automate two triage steps (labeling + weekly digest), I will recover ~1.5h/week for deep work. (Measure: time saved via calendar + task log).
3) If I set a single weekly "office hour" instead of scattered syncs, meeting overhead decreases and docs shipped increases.

Concrete steps this week:
- Block 3 x 90m focus sessions on Mon/Wed/Thu mornings; mark calendar "do not book" and share with team. (Calendar: recurring weekly 09:30-11:00)
- Finish rewrite of inbox filters and create a weekly triage digest (automation draft: inbox-filter-v2).
- Ask SRE to review on-call thresholds and propose a 24-hr backoff for non-critical alerts (linked INF-482).
- Cancel one recurring sync and propose 60m consolidated sync on Wed.
- Draft short one-pager on reducing context switches for product infra team; share by Friday.

Metrics capture plan (lightweight):
- End-of-week self-report numbers for the 5 signals above in this doc.
- Quick timer-style logging for focus sessions (start/end + interruptions).
- PR numbers from GitHub weekly activity.

Retrospective notes (end of week):
- The calendar batching change lowered perceived context switching but didn't increase total focus hours because pager fired. Pager mitigation is higher priority than calendar micro-optimizations.
- The GH action for labeling paid off — reviewers saw clearer queues. Need to iterate on labels to avoid over-tagging.

To follow up (next week):
- Sync with SRE (15m) and propose a small playbook for non-critical alerts.
- Deploy inbox digest and evaluate time saved.
- Run one deep-read (paper/blog) on inference runtime batching; jot 3 actionable notes and share.

Loose ideas / prompts to self:
- What would it take to reduce PR merge lead time to 12h consistently? Do I need a "merge hour"?
- Can I combine the docs I write into a weekly "notes thread" to reduce context switching on reading?
- Is there a small automation that can triage meeting invites to allow only those tagged with a priority 2+ to land in my calendar?

Quick links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/okrs-personal-template
- Jira ticket: INF-482 (on-call threshold)
- Github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-notes/pull/789
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02ABCD1234/p1670000000000

Notes to self (two-line): keep the signal set narrow; put experiments behind clear measurable success criteria; be ruthless with meetings for 4 weeks then reassess.

Next review: 2026-03-16 (quick 20m check-in)

-- end of scratch --
